adversarial_probes.description: Two tenants masking the SAME classified value via the 'hash' transform produce the SAME digest (digest() is keyless djb2 over the value only; tenant_id never enters maskFields/applyTransform/digest).
adversarial_probes.detail: applyTransform(v,'hash') is a pure function of v with no tenant salt. maskFields/applyTransform/digest take no tenant_id. Cross-tenant equality of values is therefore observable from masked output (equality oracle), and the 8-byte djb2 digest is brute-forceable for low-entropy values (rainbow/dictionary). Spec §6-A #12 scopes out key custody/tokenization key mgmt but does NOT require the hash transform to be tenant-scoped or salted to prevent the equality oracle — so this is a design gap surfaced, not an AC violation. Reverted.

adversarial_probes.description: partial transform on 1-4 char values must not reveal plaintext; check the >4 boundary.
adversarial_probes.detail: Values length 1..4 => '****' (fully masked, no plaintext slice) — correct. Length 5 => '****2345' reveals last 4 of 5 chars (a 5-char secret leaks 80% of itself); length 6 => '****3456'. This is the documented last-4 contract (data-classification.ts:131-132 'value.length <= 4 => ****'); for >4 the last-4 reveal is by design (partial == last-4). No AC violation: AC-5 requires only deeply-different-from-raw, which holds. Noted as inherent property of last-4 partial. Reverted.

adversarial_probes.description: governed=true + clearance=restricted (max) + a field whose class is corrupt/unresolvable => drop (not reveal). (No DataClass exists above the 'restricted' max, so the over-max case maps to corrupt/unknown class.)
adversarial_probes.detail: maskFields with governed:true, clearance:'restricted', corrupt class 'ultra-secret' => key 'ssn' omitted, raw '123456789' absent from output. selectTransform(corrupt, 'restricted') => 'drop'. Doubt resolves to maximal mask even at max clearance — NF-3 holds. Reverted.

adversarial_probes.description: resolveFor (agent path) === resolveHandle (human path) bit-for-bit on the SAME input, with REAL masking (not just identity).
adversarial_probes.detail: On a governed record {ssn:restricted, card:confidential}, clearance=internal: BOTH paths return {ssn:'[redacted]', card:'****1111'} (ssn gap2=>redact, card gap1=>partial last-4). human.toEqual(agent) AND JSON.stringify(human)===JSON.stringify(agent). Single-projection invariant verified live end-to-end through resolveFor, not just structurally. Reverted.

adversarial_probes.description: A ClassificationSource whose getClassifications throws must fail closed (never fall through to a raw projection).
adversarial_probes.verdict: pass (no raw leak); minor robustness observation
adversarial_probes.detail: A throwing getClassifications causes resolveFor to PROPAGATE the exception ('boom') rather than catching it and returning raw — raw '123456789' never surfaces. Security posture is correct (no leak). Observation: the fail-closed mode here is fail-by-crash (the read errors) rather than fail-closed-to-drop (a denied/masked result). Acceptable for a security node; flagged as a robustness note, not a defect. Reverted.

findings.severity: low-to-medium (spec-silent design gap, not AC violation)
findings.title: Keyless hash transform is a cross-tenant value-equality oracle + brute-forceable
findings.detail: The 'hash' transform digests the value with a keyless, salt-free djb2 (8-byte output) and never sees tenant_id. Identical values masked under different tenants yield identical digests => an observer of masked hashed output can detect when two tenants hold the same value (e.g. same SSN/email) and can rainbow/dictionary-attack low-entropy values. Spec §6-A #12 scopes out key custody but does not address the equality-oracle/salting question. Recommend: surface to architect — either (a) per-tenant salt threaded into digest (tenant_id is available at the resolver before maskFields, would need plumbing into MaskContext), or (b) an explicit ADR note that hash is a deterministic equality-preserving token by design and the equality oracle is accepted (matching the deferral of crypto custody to a later task). Either way the gap should be a recorded decision, not silent.

findings.title: Throwing ClassificationSource fails closed by propagating the exception, not by masking to drop
findings.detail: If getClassifications throws, resolveFor does not catch it; the request errors. Security is preserved (no raw leak), but the fail-closed mode is fail-by-crash rather than a clean denied/maximally-masked result. The port contract (§10.4) says a source that cannot determine governance MUST return governed:true — but that contract assumes the source returns; it is silent on a source that throws. Minor: a future Postgres DAO that transiently errors would surface as a hard error rather than a fail-closed mask. Recommend architect note on the throwing-source contract for T-0053.
